REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - SEPTEMBER 12, 2019 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. 11.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, requests may be made of the staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item.
12.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
SEPTEMBER 12, 2019, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Jeff Ludington, Generations Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Cerritos Recreation Services Division Youth
  Sports Scorekeepers Jayden Thomas and Tyler Gattoc.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards was excused from the meeting by
  unanimous consensus of the City Council.

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  City Clerk/Treasurer Vida Barone provided a brief update on upcoming election
  activities.

5A.  Presentations

  None.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Roger Kline expressed concern regarding truck traffic in the community.

  Mark Gross expressed concern regarding truck traffic in the community.

  Artellia Johnson requested the lease of the former Mullikin medical building be
  placed on a future agenda.

  Anna Titus spoke in support of the proposed statue honoring the City's first
  responders.

  Daisy Lagasca spoke regarding the hazards of vaping, expressed concerns with
  coyotes in the community, requested the establishment of a Youth Commission,
  and encouraged support of local school Parent Teacher Student Associations.

  Joe Duran spoke in support of the proposed statue honoring the City's first
  responders.

  Larry Lisse spoke in support of the proposed statue honoring the City's first

  Janet Duga expressed concern with homeless individuals near her business in

  Kuinso Olaja, representing the International Women's Peace Group, requested
  support to promote peace education in the community.

  Kelli Guess, representing the International Women's Peace Group, requested a
  support letter from the City Council to acknowledge the organization's peace

  Coleen Aldrich expressed concern with coyotes in the community and requested
  an item be placed on a future agenda for consideration.

  Garry Aldrich expressed concern with coyotes in the community and requested an
  item be placed on a future agenda for consideration.

  CW Van der Linden expressed concern regarding coyotes in the community.

  Emily Chen-Durnell requested extra funding for the Cerritos Tot Lot Program for
  the purpose of purchasing insurance coverage to continue the program. She
  submitted a petition for the record.

  Roger Garrett spoke in support of the proposed statue honoring the City's first
  responders.

  Ritu Gupta expressed concerns regarding truck traffic in the community.

  Mike Vinnani expressed concerns regarding coyotes in the community.

  Dixie Primosch expressed concerns regarding coyotes in the community.

  Sam Desai expressed concerns regarding coyotes in the community, the City
  Treasurer position, term limits, anti-censorship, conference attendance, and
  district elections.

  Raymond Kim expressed concerns regarding coyotes, crime, and congestion
  issues in the community.

  Mark Gross expressed concerns regarding coyotes in the community.

  Officer Michael Sherman, Long Beach Animal Control, spoke regarding the animal
  control services they provide to Cerritos by agreement, and their established
  coyote management program.

  Debbie Hamilton expressed concerns regarding coyotes in the community.

  CONSENSUS (Solanki): Directed staff to prepare a report related to options for
  addressing coyote issues in the community.

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of

  AYES:  Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki

  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of award of contract for construction of asphalt
  improvements on 183rd Street, Project No. 20302, Bid No. 1379-19 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Hu, to:

  1.  Award a contract in the amount of $504,580 (this includes an estimated amount
  of $153,000 towards improvements to be completed within the cities of Artesia
  and Lakewood) for Construction of Asphalt Improvements on 183rd Street (base
  bid plus alternates 1, 2, 3, & 4), Project No. 20302, Bid No. 1379-19, to Hardy &
  Harper, Inc., and reject the other bids; and

  2.  Authorize the City Manager to approve and execute the associated project
  participation agreement with the City of Artesia; and

  3.  Authorize the City Manager to approve and execute the associated project
  participation agreement with the City of Lakewood; and

  4.  Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related
  change orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Edwards (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of award of contract for the modification of the traffic
  signal at Bloomfield Avenue and 166th Street, Federal Project No. HSIPL-
  5325(017), Project No. 18401, Bid No. 1376-19 (COUNCIL).

  Councilmember Pulido recused himself from consideration of this item. He left his
  seat on the dais and exited the City Council Chamber.

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.
 City of Cerritos  September 12, 2019
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 6

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Yokoyama, to:

  1. Award a contract for the modification of the traffic signal at Bloomfield Avenue
  and 166th Street, Federal Project No. HSIPL-5325(017), Project No. 18401, Bid
  No. 1376-19, in the amount of $263,401, (base bid plus alternate #1), to
  Crosstown Electrical & Data, Inc., and reject the other bids; and

  2. Award a contract for construction inspection services for the modification of the
  traffic signal at Bloomfield Avenue and 166th Street, Federal Project No. HSIPL-
  5325(017), Project No. 18401, RFP No. 1369-19, in the amount of $21,960, to
  GK & Associates; and

  3. Amend the contract awarded to W.G. Zimmerman Engineering (awarded
  February 22, 2018, RFP No. 1332-18) in the amount of $8,778.00 for
  construction support and administration of the modification of the traffic signal at
  Bloomfield Avenue and 166th Street, Federal Project No. HSIPL-5325(017),
  Project No. 18401, Bid No. 1376-19; and

  4. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related
  change orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (3 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Edwards (excused), Pulido (recused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

  At the conclusion of this item Councilmember Pulido returned to the City Council
  Chamber and resumed his seat on the dais.

9C.  Review and consideration of award of contract for Cerritos parkway tree
  maintenance, RFB No. 1378-19 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Todd Kuh, Parks Superintendent. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Yokoyama, to:

  1. Award a contract for Cerritos parkway tree maintenance, RFB No. 1378-19, in
  the amount of $680,800.00 to BrightView Tree Care Services, Inc.; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related
  change orders, which may include additional trimming in the current fiscal year
  and additional grid trimming projects in the amounts of $635,201, $771,786,
  and $784,800 should the City Council allocate funding for tree trimming in the
  2020-21, 2021-22, and 2022-23 fiscal years, respectively (COUNCIL).
